description: Snyk CLI scans and monitors your projects for security vulnerabilities.
vibe: Map the binary first, then chase the bug to the repo that actually owns it.
highlights: Treats the CLI as a binary container composed from external extension repos, making ownership boundaries explicit before any debugging or coding begins.
Documents command routing and the legacy TypeScript fallback so agents understand why some commands work without a Go workflow.
Defines a strict environment-variable allowlist and prefix contract, preventing invisible config reads and accidental public API changes.
Requires local multi-repo development through go mod replace and restricts builds to make build to avoid error-prone build paths.
Layers testing by unit, integration, and acceptance scope, with a pre-commit format/lint/no-drift gate that mirrors CI.
assessment: This is effective because it attacks the highest-risk failure mode in a multi-repo CLI: agents editing the wrong repository or misdiagnosing product behavior as host plumbing. The env-var allowlist and prefix table turn configuration into an explicit contract rather than a pile of ambient process state. The build and pre-commit rules are pragmatic guardrails that keep local work aligned with CI without overprescribing implementation details.
